acceptance: Regression tests with a stubbed runner: during a wait that a reused read would otherwise pass, each of the following appearing mid-wait still prevents the arm on the next cycle: a hold label, a red trunk, a new unresolved review thread, a newly required check, and a head change.
A test shows the arming attempt performs every read fresh: the stub records each endpoint read in that attempt.
A test shows a cycle that is waiting on a named CI run performs only that run's status read and the trunk gate, and that a failed narrow read falls back to the full chain.

Before and after, on one real `make pr-arm WAIT=` wait of at least 5 cycles, the requests per cycle are counted (with GH_DEBUG=api or `X-RateLimit-Used` deltas, no other sessions active) and recorded on this item. Phase 1 merges only if the count per waiting cycle drops.
Phase 2 is either merged with its own before-and-after measurement, or recorded as dropped with the probe result.
Existing `tests/unit/scripts/test_pr_arm*` and the `pr_landing` tests pass, and the arming outcome lines are unchanged.
context: 2026-11-17 adversarial review against live origin/develop. Rewrote the description and acceptance. Main defect fixed: the original plan cached the trunk state for up to half of WAIT, which would let a pull request arm while develop had turned red, loosening a gate the item itself said not to change. Also fixed: `gh pr view` is GraphQL and cannot use ETags; the tracker index is read at a fixed SHA and needs no ETag; `gh api` exits 1 on 304 and `--jq`/`--paginate` drop the ETag; whether a 304 is free was not established; the 16%/44% estimates assumed the now-forbidden trunk caching and counted processes, not requests; the code has no cross-cycle state, so the change is larger than described; the acceptance did not test that mid-wait refusals still apply.
description:
Remedy (a) chosen by the owner on 2026-11-17 for shared-github-quota-and-transient-failure-owner-20261113. A 26-hour measurement (2026-11-15 to 2026-11-16) found about 30,000 core REST requests, one hourly window at the 5,000 limit, and `scripts/pr_arm.py` starting 65% of observed `gh` processes (5,886 of 9,040) from 14 concurrent worktrees. Per wait cycle it repeats: the paginated check-runs read (1,566 processes in 26 h), `gh run list --workflow trunk.yml` via the trunk gate (860), the ruleset required-checks read (590), the paginated ci-text-edit-refresh workflow-runs read (549), the tracker index read (373) and `gh pr view` (281). These are process counts, not request counts: paginated reads are several requests each.

How the live code works (origin/develop, 2026-11-17). `arm_waiting` keeps no state between cycles. Each cycle sleeps 180 s, calls `trunk_gate()` (`trunk_revert.arm_gate`), then re-runs all of `arm()`: `gh pr view` (GraphQL), review threads, `suite_refusals`, the duration verdict, `visible_refusals`, the review gate, batch and stale-base checks. The ruleset read (`pr_landing.ruleset_required_contexts`) and the check-runs read (`pr_landing.live_check_runs`) are each called from several of those functions, so one cycle reads them more than once. The tracker index is read at a pinned state-branch SHA (`contents/index.json?ref=<tip_sha>`).

Safety invariant (binding). A read reused from an earlier cycle may only ever produce a `waiting` outcome. The attempt that arms runs every check from fresh reads, exactly as today. Therefore a hold label, a red trunk, a new unresolved thread or a changed required check that appears during a wait still refuses the arm.

Phase 1 (first pull request).
1. Within one cycle, read each source once: pass the ruleset contexts and check-run records to the functions that currently re-read them.
2. While the latest outcome is waiting, re-poll only the conditions named in the waiting reasons (for example the status of the CI run `waiting for full CI run <id>` names, or the review-verdict status), plus the trunk gate every cycle. When every waiting condition has cleared, or the head changes, run the full fresh chain. If that chain still says waiting, continue polling.
3. Cache the tracker index by state-branch SHA: content at a fixed SHA cannot change, so only the branch-tip read is repeated.

Phase 2 (separate pull request, only if decision gate 2 passes). Conditional requests (If-None-Match) for the remaining polled REST reads.

Decision gates.
1. Before phase 1 code: list every refusal kind `arm()` can return and map each to the narrowest read that shows it cleared. A waiting reason with no such narrow read falls back to the full chain each cycle.
2. Before phase 2: establish whether a 304 counts against the primary rate limit for this user. Probe on 2026-11-17: six consecutive 304s on the ruleset endpoint moved `X-RateLimit-Used` by 3 while other sessions were active, so the result is inconclusive. Repeat with no other sessions running, or drop phase 2 and record why. Also note: `gh api` exits 1 on a 304, and `--jq` and `--paginate` discard headers and ETags, so conditional reads need `gh api -i` and their own parsing, with one ETag per page for paginated endpoints. `gh pr view` uses GraphQL, which has no ETags, so it is not a candidate.
3. Any change to which checks must pass, the review-gate rules or the trunk-gate rules is out of scope: stop and report.
4. Deliver together with pr-arm-github-rate-limit-backoff-20261112 only if both change the same read helper. Either way it ships serially, because `pr-arm` is a landing tool.

Expected saving: not estimated. The earlier 16% figure assumed the trunk read could be cached, which the invariant forbids, and it counted processes, not requests. Measure instead (see acceptance).

Out of scope, recorded for later. Each of the 14 concurrent worktrees polls the same develop-wide state (trunk runs, ruleset, tracker index). A cache shared across sessions would save more, but it adds cross-process staleness and needs its own design. `scripts/trunk_revert.py` (551 processes of its own) and the 24% of calls from hand polling are also not covered here.

Guardrails.
- The safety invariant above.
- An unreadable read is never a pass. A failed narrow poll falls back to the full fresh chain, never to a stale result.
- The number of GitHub requests per cycle only goes down. No request is added.
- No credentials, tokens or identities change.
- No check is skipped or made non-blocking.
- Tests use a stubbed runner. None calls GitHub.
